headline: I build the
that let teams ship software with AI.
hero.lede: Staff software engineer, ten years building end-to-end platforms. I work on developer experience and architecture — integrations, internal tooling, and how a team puts AI into its own development.

process.statement: The interesting part isn’t writing code faster. It’s the workflow a whole team ships on.
paragraphs: Claude Code wired into Jira and Figma over MCP, GitHub CLI automation, custom skills for auditing, documentation and component generation, and layered repository rules with maintained memory. Work moves from ticket to pull request through plain language and a few links.
It holds up on Adobe Experience Manager, a stack current models have almost no training coverage of.

What changes when this works is the constraint. Pull request volume doubled and the median time to merge held — but so did the number of changes reaching the main branch with nobody reviewing them. It stops being how fast code gets written and becomes how fast it can be read.

cards.title: An enterprise AEM platform, and the workflow the team shipped it with.
facts: Joined a build already in flight; little had shipped
Component libraries behind the full template set, multi-language authoring
Okta, Stripe, and a multi-step transactional flow across 6–7 complex page types
10–15 active developers at a time, in a programme of around sixty across engineering, QA, product and management
Two other agent frameworks tried and dropped before this one held
cards.outcome: I worked on the platform itself — templates, components and integrations — and brought agent-based development into the main repository, then maintained it as eight other engineers built on it. Half the team was shipping AI-assisted work within six months.

cards.title: An authoring pipeline that ran on paste.
facts: The application delivering Forrester’s research to its clients
Custom Contentful app converting Word research templates into rich text with custom components
Authors used to copy approved documents into the CMS by hand and rebuild the formatting
cards.outcome: I built the Contentful app behind it — Word template in, structured rich text and components out.

clients.lede: Clients I’ve built for, across finance, hospitality, research, insurance and government — platforms I owned architecture and delivery on, not logos I passed through.

paragraphs: A decade in agencies, delivering for finance, insurance, automotive, hospitality and research — from small sites to enterprise platforms, as developer, team lead and tech lead. The work I’m best at is
: architecture, integrations, and the standards a team builds against.

Building the tooling a team runs on is the work I want more of. I’ve spent my career in rooms with clients, authoring teams and stakeholders, translating between what people need and what actually gets built.

I studied American Culture and Literature before I wrote code professionally, which is probably why I end up doing as much explaining as engineering. I work best where communication is direct and people are treated with respect.
